tasks.short: Assign the daily station maintenance tasks, take part in checking vehicles and equipment, check that tasks are done, and record equipment checks.

steps.what: Fire captain directs firefighters in station maintenance duties by assigning the day's tasks
Fire captain participates in maintenance of vehicles and equipment
Firefighters tick each check in the app after scanning the item's QR code
Fire captain checks that maintenance tasks are done
Fire captain records equipment checks on paper lists

tasks.design: A station maintenance app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) holds recurring checks per vehicle and piece of equipment; a QR code on each opens its checklist, and the captain sees done and open tasks on one screen instead of walking round with paper lists. Assigning tasks and doing maintenance with the crew stay with the captain; task logs are kept per item, not used to rate firefighters.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checks were planned from memory and ticked on paper lists in the station.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance apps with QR checklists are common in fleets and stations.
tasks.still_hard: A call-out interrupts maintenance at any moment.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a pump sounds wrong during a weekly test.

evidence.claim: Maintenance apps can hold recurring checklists opened by QR code on each item.
Systems that can monitor staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the maintenance schedule to the check record; repairs by the workshop are outside.
Input contract: check intervals set by the safety region's equipment department; fallback is paper lists.

Firefighters tick checks in the app in about the time paper took (s2f, other-role time). s1 keeps 70 because the app shows what is due and assigning stays; s3 keeps 70 because done and open tasks show on one screen; s4 keeps 85 because the QR code opens the right checklist and the captain still records each check.

incremental.description: Fire captain keeps checklists current after equipment changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small station with one vehicle, so walking round took little and s1 and s3 keep 90 (4.8); high: a large station with many vehicles and items (10.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe drills and routines, review turnout times and incident data, compare procedures with departmental regulations, write the evaluation, send it to the station commander, and discuss findings with the crew.

steps.what: Fire captain observes drills and daily routines
Fire captain reviews turnout times and incident data in a spreadsheet
Fire captain looks up the departmental regulations that apply to each procedure
Fire captain evaluates fire station procedures against departmental regulations
Fire captain writes the evaluation and proposals

loop.input: The captain's findings, the turnout figures and the regulation texts referred to.
loop.output: A draft evaluation note with findings and proposals.
loop.check: Each finding must quote the regulation article or the figure it rests on, or it is dropped; the captain reads each finding against its quote to check the quote supports it, edits the note and writes unclear findings by hand.
loop.stop: Stops when the captain approves, or after two redrafts the captain writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Findings need short explanations in prose; a template only lists headings.

steps.what: Fire captain checks the final evaluation: findings against observations, figures and regulations, the proposals, and the station commander it goes to
Fire captain sends the checked evaluation to the station commander
Fire captain discusses the findings with the crew

tasks.design: A dashboard ({BI}) from the incident registration shows turnout times and incident data per station and shift, replacing spreadsheet exports. Departmental regulations sit in one searchable document system with versions. A bounded step drafts the evaluation note; every finding must quote its regulation article or figure, and the captain edits. The captain checks the final note and sends it once to the station commander. Observing drills and discussing with the crew stay with the captain; turnout data are shown per crew, not used to rate individuals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incident data were exported to spreadsheets and regulations searched in several folders.
tasks.enabler_now: Incident dashboards and document systems with versions are common in safety regions.
tasks.still_hard: Procedures that work on paper can fail under stress.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing in a drill that a procedure slows the crew down.
tasks.altitude: The captain reads dashboards and edits drafts instead of compiling data and writing from scratch.

evidence.claim: Dashboards can show turnout times from incident registration per station and shift.
Systems that can monitor staff need works council consent; effects of public tasks on staff work are a council matter.

assumptions: Boundary: from station routines to the crew informed; regional policy is outside.
Input contract: incident data from the region's registration; regulations from the region's document system; fallback is exports and folders.

Observing, evaluating, discussing and the final check do not change. s5 keeps 70 because the draft lays out findings with their quotes and the captain still writes the proposals; s6 keeps 25 for the send.
No personal data of victims go into the drafting step.

already_counted.description: Fire captain edits and approves the drafted note.

incremental.description: Fire captain checks dashboard figures against the logbook.

approvals.approved_version: The evaluation note with findings and proposals exactly as checked by the captain in s5b, sent once to the station commander; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few evaluations with little incident data, so s2 keeps 70 and s5 keeps 90 (15.1); high: regular evaluations with much incident data (24.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read updates to fire regulations and guidance, attend training and exercises, discuss tactics with colleagues after incidents, and look up rules when questions come up.

steps.what: Fire captain reads updates to fire laws and guidance
Fire captain maintains knowledge of fire prevention techniques and tactics through training and exercises
Fire captain discusses tactics with colleagues after incidents
Fire captain looks up rules when a question comes up

tasks.design: The safety region's document system ({DOCS}) sends alerts when a regulation or guideline the region applies changes, with a short summary of what changed, and the current texts are searchable in one place with the article shown. Training, exercises and discussing tactics stay with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes were spread over newsletters and rules searched in several folders.
tasks.enabler_now: Document systems with change alerts and full-text search are common.
tasks.still_hard: New tactics are learned by practice, not reading.
tasks.human_edge: Translating a new guideline into what the crew does at the door.

reach.learn: Whether captains find current rules faster.

evidence.claim: Document systems can send alerts on changes and search current texts.
Safety regions apply PGS 15 for stored hazardous substances in permit procedures; version 1.1 dates from April 2026.

assumptions: Boundary: from regulation updates to rules found; writing regulations is outside.
Input contract: texts and changes kept by the region's document team; fallback is newsletters and folders.
Training, exercises and discussions do not change.
research_questions: Do captains apply new rules sooner?

incremental.description: Fire captain reports outdated texts to the document team.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few rule changes in a year and summaries too short to rely on, so s1 keeps 90 and s4 keeps 80 (5.5); high: a year with many changed guidelines (14.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect crew feedback on equipment, gather fault and repair history, compare products, write the recommendation, send it to the equipment committee, and present it.

steps.what: Fire captain collects crew feedback on equipment
Fire captain gathers fault and repair history of the equipment
Fire captain compares products and specifications
Fire captain writes the recommendation for equipment modifications or new purchases
Fire captain checks the final recommendation: need, options, costs and repair history against the sources, and the committee it goes to
Fire captain sends the checked recommendation to the equipment committee
Fire captain presents the recommendation to the committee

tasks.design: The station maintenance app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows fault and repair history per item, so the captain does not compile it. Recommendations use a fixed template with need, options, costs and the repair history pulled in. The captain checks the finished recommendation and sends it once to the equipment committee from the document space ({DOCS}). Hearing the crew, comparing products and presenting stay with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repair history was gathered from workshop e-mails and recommendations written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance apps keep repair history per item; templates structure recommendations.
tasks.still_hard: Budgets decide more than evidence does.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which tool the crew trusts in smoke and darkness.

reach.learn: Whether recommendations come with repair data.

evidence.claim: Maintenance apps can show repair history per item; templates can pull it into a document.

assumptions: Boundary: from equipment problems to the recommendation presented; buying is outside.
Input contract: repair history from the maintenance app; fallback is workshop e-mails.

Crew feedback, comparing, presenting and the final check do not change. s2 keeps 40 for reading the history; s4 keeps 70 because the template gives the layout and the repair history and the captain writes the argument; s5 keeps 25 for the send.
Committee members' time does not change.
research_questions: Do recommendations get decided at the first meeting more often?

incremental.description: Fire captain keeps the recommendation template current.

approvals.approved_version: The recommendation with need, options and costs exactly as checked by the captain in s4b, sent once to the equipment committee from the document space; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a simple purchase with little repair history in the app, so s2 keeps 70 and s4 keeps 85 (11.7); high: a large purchase with long repair history (21.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The fire captain keeps leading maintenance, judging procedures, training and hearing the crew; paper lists, spreadsheet exports, folder searches and blank-page notes shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A captain with more time for drills and the crew.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Firefighting and Prevention Workers
